knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A partly completed agreed task is recorded as an exclusion with the reason, so the owner can see what was not done. Recording it as complete, or leaving it off the record, hides the gap. Completed work is reported separately from outstanding items, and the property is never described as fully safe.
Completed work and the urgent electrical referral are reported separately.
Corrections are dated additions so the original record is preserved.

practicalCriteria: instructions: Prepare a final handover with evidence photos, task acceptance, outstanding hazards and referral details.; evidence required: Prepare a completed-work checklist with photos, exclusions and follow-on trade referrals.; supervision: Competent supervisor; no unlicensed regulated work
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 1: Compare the completed work with the signed scope, item by item.
Record of procedure step 2: Check the products were used as the manufacturer instructions say, and record the products used.
Record of procedure step 3: Record completed items, exclusions and referrals in three separate lists.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 3 is not done: Record completed items, exclusions and referrals in three separate lists.
Stop work if procedure step 5 is not done: Hand over to the client, stating what is done, what is not, and what needs referral.
